question: In the valid (and train) split, what fraction of users have BOTH a long_view=1 and a long_view=0 row (i.e. can contribute a non-trivial ranking comparison to GAUC), what fraction of users have all-same-label rows (contributing no ranking signal), what's the median/mean number of rows per user, and what fraction of users have fewer than 5 valid rows (meaning nDCG@5 is trivially saturated/underdetermined for them)? This tells us whether the primary metric's sensitivity is bottlenecked by a small pool of "informative" users, which would explain why structurally different mechanisms keep landing within ~0.002-0.007 of each other.
reflection: My last iteration spent the web-research budget confirming Dynamic Negative Sampling (DNS) is a plausible lever, but didn't test any code, so it didn't move the plateau. Given 5 of the last 6 code-level changes (across negative_sampling, training_procedure, model_architecture, multi_task, popularity_debiasing) all landed within ~0.001-0.007 of the same 0.604 ceiling regardless of mechanism, I suspect the metric itself has a small "effective" sample of users that actually drives GAUC/nDCG@5 — i.e. most of these deltas may be within noise of the evaluation set's own limited discriminative power, not real signal differences between mechanisms.
